title: Choose the visual world for QR Studio
question: The roll assigned the Annotated Spec Drawing. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Annotated Spec Drawing
options.lineage: ISO technical drawings and standards datasheets (the ISO/IEC 18004 QR figures)
options.thesis: Every code ships as its own engineering drawing: dimensioned, annotated and checked before it leaves the sheet.
materials: colour-coded CAD layers in GDG blue, red, yellow, green
options.viewport: A full-bleed drawing sheet: the headline set large at top-left, a live QR at centre-right with leaders calling out the finder patterns, the 4-module quiet zone and the encoded payload typing into a callout, and the title block bottom-right carrying Built for GDG on Campus SRM and the Open Studio action.
options.risk: Turns into blueprint cliché if rendered blue-on-blue, or cold if annotations become decoration instead of real measurements.

raised.raise: Measurements are interface: contrast ratio, quiet zone, bytes and ECC recovery get fixed-width tabular readouts, not chips.
The encoded payload and module matrix appear at true data density beside the code, never as decoration.
One input propagates: typing a payload re-dimensions every annotation on the sheet at once.
A strict, small type scale: rank carried by weight, case and rule, not by many sizes.
Modules that change when the payload morphs leave a brief highlight trace, then settle.

options.label: DevFest Badge System
options.lineage: GDG and DevFest attendee badges, lanyards and check-in desks
options.thesis: Every code is an attendee badge: a printed card with a check-in QR, a colour role and a lanyard.
options.viewport: The live code hangs as a badge on a lanyard in the hero, swaying gently; each QR type is a badge colour role and the headline reads like the event name.
options.risk: The closest to where most event-site runs land; badge mockups read as a conference template if the system stops at the hero.

options.label: Pop Sleeve Releases
options.thesis: Five QR types as five releases, each on its own flat GDG-colour ground.
options.viewport: One flat blue field, the live code cropped large like a portrait, the five types listed small as tracks in the corner.
options.case: Fuses well and wins audience identification through the GDG colours; loses product clarity because it cannot show payload formats or measurements.
options.risk: Saturated grounds fight the contrast story; every code needs a white plate.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: The code as a pure black-and-white data field.
options.viewport: A wall of bars with the code resolving out of it.
options.case: Breaks the GDG colour commitment and loses audience identification.
options.kept: Data-density courage: the real payload and matrix shown at true density.
options.risk: Strobing and pure B/W conflict with the brand and accessibility.

options.label: Nixie Lab Counter
options.thesis: Contrast ratio and byte counts glow as instrument digits.
options.viewport: Banks of tubes reading 17.7:1 beside the code.
options.case: Dramatises measurement but cannot show encoding; weaker audience fit.
options.kept: Quantities are the interface, each with fixed digit positions.
options.risk: Dark glow undercuts the scannability message.

options.label: Miura-fold Sheet
options.thesis: The code unfolds from a packet into a full sheet.
options.viewport: A packet pulled open into the code.
options.case: No link to the audience; the fold says nothing about scanning.
options.kept: One control propagates across the whole sheet.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight, case and rule.
options.case: Beautiful discipline, wrong world for students making posters.
options.risk: Raked layout fights the tool's forms.

options.label: Bioluminescent Wake
options.thesis: Modules glow where the pointer passes.
options.viewport: A dark field the pointer lights up.
options.case: Low contrast contradicts the product's core warning.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS-style generator landing page, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and CTA on the left, a framed screenshot of the studio on the right, then a feature grid and FAQ.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other QR generator by design.
